Manakin Town
man'a-kin town
n. (the Huguenot settlement on the James River in Virginia, founded 1700)
From Monacan, the Siouan people whose abandoned village stood on the site; anglicised as Manakin.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Manakin Town was the chief Huguenot settlement in Virginia, planted in 1700 and 1701 some twenty miles above the falls of the James River, on the site of a deserted Monacan village. Between six and seven hundred refugees came in four shiploads, sent from England where they had gathered after the Revocation, with William III's encouragement and a grant of ten thousand acres; the Virginia Assembly exempted them from taxes for seven years and set them up as King William Parish, a French-speaking parish within the established church of the colony. The first years were very hard: the land was poor for wheat, the mortality was heavy, and the settlers petitioned repeatedly for relief. They turned to tobacco and to vine-growing, intermarried with their English neighbours, and within two generations the parish was English-speaking and the names — Maury, Flournoy, Dupuy, Michaux, Trabue — had become Virginian. “By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country” (Heb 11:9).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines to sojourn as to dwell for a time, and a plantation as a colony or the place where a colony is settled.

expand to see more

PLANTA'TION, n. The place planted; a colony; an original settlement in a new country.

SO'JOURN, v. To dwell for a time; to live in a place as a temporary resident or as a stranger.

PAR'ISH, n. The precinct or territorial jurisdiction of a secular priest, or the people under his care.

WIL'DERNESS, n. A desert; a tract of land or region uncultivated and uninhabited.

Key Scripture

Heb 11:9 — "By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:"

Gen 12:1 — "Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee:"

Psa 107:4 — "They wandered in the wilderness in a solitary way; they found no city to dwell in."

Psa 107:7 — "And he led them forth by the right way, that they might go to a city of habitation."

Modern Corruption

Seven hundred Huguenots on the James River, English-speaking within two generations.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The live misuse is the genealogical romance that has grown around Manakin Town, in which the settlement is remembered chiefly as the origin of distinguished Virginian families and the first decade's destitution drops out. The parish records and the petitions to the Assembly are plain about what it cost; a good many of those who landed did not survive the second winter.

The principle to recover is that the patriarchal life of faith was a life without a settled title, and that Scripture treats this as the normal shape of the pilgrim's condition rather than as a misfortune: “By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles” (Heb 11:9). The psalm of the redeemed begins exactly where Manakin Town began — “They wandered in the wilderness in a solitary way; they found no city to dwell in” (Psa 107:4) — and does not stay there: “And he led them forth by the right way, that they might go to a city of habitation” (Psa 107:7).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek paroikeo (G3939), to sojourn, dwell as a stranger; Hebrew taah (H8582), to wander.

Greek paroikeo (G3939) — to dwell beside, sojourn as a stranger; Hebrews 11:9.

Greek allotrios (G245) — belonging to another, strange, foreign; Hebrews 11:9.

Hebrew taah (H8582) — to wander, stray, go astray; Psalm 107:4.

Hebrew yeshimon (H3452) — a desert, wilderness, waste; Psalm 107:4.

Hebrew moshab (H4186) — a dwelling place, habitation; Psalm 107:7.

Usage

"“he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country” (Heb 11:9) — King William Parish, 1700."

"“Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred” (Gen 12:1) — four shiploads out of France by way of England."

"“they found no city to dwell in” (Psa 107:4) — the first winters above the falls."
